# 9.4 Reduction in taxable value where expenditure would have been deductible to the employee
The taxable value of an expense payment fringe benefit may be reduced in accordance with the otherwise deductible rule, but only if the recipient of the benefit is the employee.

Under the otherwise deductible rule, if you reimbursed the employee for all or part of this expense, the taxable value of the expense payment fringe benefit would be nil.

# 9.9 Common expenses reimbursed or paid for by employers
## Self-education expenses
This is an expense payment fringe benefit.

The taxable value is the amount you pay. If the self-education expenses are work related, the taxable value can be reduced by the otherwise deductible rule (refer to section [9.4](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22SAV%2FFBTGEMP%2F9.4%22&PiT=99991231235958#9.4) ). # Expense payment fringe benefits
## What is an expense payment fringe benefit?
### Changes to salary sacrificed work-related expense payment fringe benefits from 1 April 2027
#### What's changing?
Currently, you can use the [otherwise deductible rule](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/exemptions-concessions-and-other-ways-to-reduce-fbt/reducing-your-fbt-liability#ato-Providingbenefitsthatwouldbedeductiblefortheemployee) to reduce your FBT liability where your employee could have claimed an income tax deduction for the expense if they paid for it themselves.

#### What isn't changing?
##### Example: annual self-education expense

### Reductions and concessions
You may be able to reduce the taxable value of an expense payment fringe benefit (or eliminate it entirely) if:

- the [otherwise deductible rule](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/exemptions-concessions-and-other-ways-to-reduce-fbt/reducing-your-fbt-liability#ato-Providingbenefitsthatwouldbedeductiblefortheemployee) applies – that is, if your employee could have claimed an income tax deduction for the expense if they had paid for it themselves; you must [keep records](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/expense-payment-fringe-benefits#Recordsyouneedtokeep) to support your claim

web.title: Reducing your FBT liability | Australian Taxation Office
web.description:
# Reducing your FBT liability
## Providing benefits that would be deductible for the employee
This is called the 'otherwise deductible' rule.

If only a proportion of the expense would have been deductible for the employee, you reduce the value of the fringe benefit by the proportion that would have been deductible.

### Example: substantiating reduction with employee declaration
- uses the 'otherwise deductible' rule to reduce the taxable value of the fringe benefit by 40%

## Using employee contributions
You can [reduce your FBT liability](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=SAV/FBTGEMP/00020&PiT=99991231235958/) by having your employee contribute towards the cost of a fringe benefit.

For most categories of fringe benefits, the taxable value of a fringe benefit can be reduced by the amount of the employee contribution.
